discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional and moiré quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees collapses the electronic bandwidth, creating nearly flat Dirac bands where interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. This opened twistronics: the twist angle became a new, continuously tunable knob for designing strongly correlated matter. Moiré systems now host superconductivity, orbital ferromagnetism, Chern insulators, Wigner crystals and, most recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states without a magnetic field. They have become one of the most widely used platforms in condensed matter physics. Optical, nano-infrared, STM and transport probes all now use moiré materials as a programmable laboratory for many-body physics. Few discoveries of the past decade have changed so deeply how we create and control quantum phases of electrons.
